message.content:
**Killing Visual Studio Code (code.exe) from the command line**

On Windows the main executable for VS Code is called **`Code.exe`** (note the capital “C”).  
If you want to terminate it from a batch file, PowerShell script, or just a quick one‑liner, you can use `taskkill`.

---

### 1️⃣ Basic “kill everything” command

```cmd
taskkill /IM Code.exe /F
```

* `/IM Code.exe` – matches the image name (`Code.exe`).  
* `/F` – forces termination (equivalent to Ctrl‑C + Ctrl‑Break).  

This will close *all* running instances of VS Code immediately.

---

### 2️⃣ Kill a specific instance (by PID)

First list the processes:

```cmd
tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq Code.exe"
```

Find the **PID** column value for the instance you want to stop, then run:

```cmd
taskkill /PID <PID_NUMBER> /F
```

Replace `<PID_NUMBER>` with the actual number.

---

### 3️⃣ Terminate the process tree (children too)

Sometimes VS Code spawns helper processes (e.g., extensions, webviews).  
To ensure those are also killed:

```cmd
taskkill /IM Code.exe /F /T
```

* `/T` – terminates the specified process and any child processes started by it.

---

### 4️⃣ Using PowerShell (alternative)

If you prefer PowerShell, the equivalent command is:

```powershell
Stop-Process -Name Code -Force
```

or for a specific PID:

```powershell
Stop-Process -Id <PID_NUMBER> -Force
```

---

### ⚠️ Things to keep in mind

| Issue | What to watch out for |
|-------|------------------------|
| **Case sensitivity** | `Code.exe` is case‑sensitive in the `/IM` switch; use the exact name. |
| **Admin rights** | Killing processes owned by other users may require elevated privileges. |
| **Unsaved work** | Force‑killing will not prompt to save unsaved files—use only when you’re sure. |
| **Multiple instances** | If you have several VS Code windows open, `/IM Code.exe /F` will close *all* of them. |

---

#### Quick cheat sheet

| Command | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `taskkill /IM Code.exe /F` | Close all VS Code windows immediately |
| `taskkill /PID <n> /F` | Close a specific instance |
| `taskkill /IM Code.exe /F /T` | Close VS Code plus any spawned child processes |
| `Stop-Process -Name Code -Force` | PowerShell equivalent of the first command |

That’s it! Use whichever form fits your workflow. Happy coding (and killing)!
